text: Hi Maria, it's Alex at Westbrook State again. Let's finish the loan part of Daniel's letter.
Sure, I've got the letter open.
Daniel's Federal Direct Unsubsidized Loan is $2,000.
Oh good, so that one won't grow at all while he's still in school.

expect.note: (i) Maria thinks the unsubsidized loan doesn't accrue interest during school; it does. Alex corrects it in his next turn after the private card.

text: Actually, it's the other way around. Interest on the unsubsidized loan starts adding up right away, even during school. Only the subsidized one has its interest covered while he's enrolled.
So do you want to keep both loans, or only the subsidized one?
Both, I think. Neither of them grows until he graduates, so there's no hurry.

expect.note: (i) Two turns after Alex's correction, Maria falls back into the same belief. It must become a second nudge (the model may reuse the resolved flag's key), not 'none'. Alex moves on, so Beacon may ask.

text: Okay. Next on the letter is the work-study award.
Thanks for flagging that. Maria, the unsubsidized loan does grow while Daniel is in school, because its interest starts as soon as the money goes out.
Oh, okay. So only the subsidized one waits until after school. Got it now.
Right. So, Daniel's Federal Work-Study award is $2,500 for the year.
That's great, so that $2,500 comes off the tuition bill right away.

expect.note: (ii) Maria thinks work-study is credited to the bill; it is paid as paychecks. She then adds three short push-to-talk presses, and Alex's next turn moves on. Counted from the card that would be stale; counted from Alex's first chance, Beacon asks.

text: Oh,
that helps a lot,
honestly.
Great. Moving on, the Westbrook Grant is $9,000 for the year.
Good question, thank you. Maria, work-study isn't taken off the bill. Daniel earns it as paychecks from a campus job, for the hours he works.
Oh, so it's his paycheck as he works. We still pay the bill ourselves.
Exactly. To keep the Westbrook Grant, Daniel needs Satisfactory Academic Progress: at least a 2.0 GPA and finishing 67 percent of the credits he attempts, every term.
Okay, so a C average, and he has to finish most of his classes each term.
That's it. Now, the Parent PLUS loan on the letter is $8,500, offered to you. And the net price is $23,000.
Oh nice, so Daniel pays that loan back once he's working.

expect.note: (iii) First of two misreads back to back: the Parent PLUS loan is the parent's to repay. Alex moves on, so Beacon asks about it; that starts the 20-second cooldown.

text: And the $23,000 is what's left after the loans come off.

expect.note: (iii) Second misread, in the very next press: net price subtracts only grants. Both are due at Alex's next turn; Beacon asks about the first, and the cooldown then holds this one until Alex clarifies it. It must still be flagged (not 'none' or 'dropped'), and never spoken.

text: Last thing on the money: accept each award in the student portal.
Right, that loan is yours to repay, Maria.
And one correction: the net price only takes off the grants. The loans still count toward it.
Oh, I see. So the $23,000 is before any loans.
Exactly. Do you have any other questions about the letter?
Yes, when do the verification papers have to be in?

expect.note: (iv) Maria asks a question, then answers it herself from the letter. No unanswered-question flag, and Beacon never asks it for her.

text: Oh never mind, I see it on the letter. July 15.
Perfect. The transcripts and the worksheet both go to our office.
We'll review them within a couple of weeks.
You'll get an email with the link.
Okay.

expect.note: (v) A 2.6-second pause and a plain 'okay' after a simple logistics sentence. Nothing to flag.

text: That's everything for today. Congratulations again to Daniel.
Thank you, Alex. Bye now.
